main_text.p: Vt, hic sunt duo Diagonalia alterum maius. b. alterum minus. a.
Diagonale est totum illud spacium quadratum, quod linea transversa secat. Diagonia f. Diagonus est ipsa linea, diagonalia secans.
Nec tantum in Parallelogrammis exacte quadratis, sed etiam in oblongis: nec tamen inæqualia, sed & æqualia diagonalia sunt, ut vides.
Complementum est particulare Parallelogrammum à conterminis diagonalium lateribus comprehensum.

Dicitur ideo complementa quia cum Diagonalibus totum parallelogrammum complent. Neque vero diagonalia duo describi possunt, quia una complementa describantur. NB. Complementa sunt æqualia; itaque si unum excedat alterum latitudine, alterum excedat longitudine. 4. p. 1.
Gnoma est alterum Diagonale cum duobus complementis. 2. d. 2.

page.notes: Figures: a diagonal/complement square with labels "a" and "b"; a label "diag." with "æqual." between brackets; a box labelled "Complementum" with a vertical "Complementum"; a parallelogram captioned "parall. quadr. oblōg."; three gnomon/L-shaped figures and a small tree-like sign at right. The word "lum" and the signature "H 3" stand at the foot of the page. Some printed words at figure edges were unclear and are transcribed as best read.
